status_summary: Public Law 119-92, the Investing in All of America Act of 2025 (H.R. 2066), approved 2026-05-19, amends section 303(b)(2) of the Small Business Investment Act so that SBICs may exclude from their outstanding leverage investments in small manufacturers, alongside small businesses in low-income or rural areas and in covered technology areas, up to the lesser of 50 percent of private capital or 125 million dollars, for investments made after enactment. The law also revises the private capital definition, adding college and university foundations, endowments and trusts and excluding most government-derived funds. SBA's final rule of 2026-01-02 (91 FR 1), effective 2026-02-02, removed obsolete provisions including Early Stage SBIC licensing and allowed financing of critical minerals projects expected to last more than 48 months, while keeping the one-year minimum and 20-year maximum financing terms. Neither the law nor the rule provides the longer-term financing for manufacturers that the chapter names, and no SBA rule implementing the new leverage exclusion was found.

timeline.event: SBA published a final rule amending 13 CFR part 107 (91 FR 1), effective 2026-02-02, removing obsolete provisions such as Early Stage SBIC licensing and allowing financing of critical minerals projects longer than 48 months.

H.R. 2066, the Investing in All of America Act of 2025, was approved as Public Law 119-92 after House passage on 2025-12-01 and Senate passage on 2026-04-15; it adds a leverage exclusion for SBIC investments in small manufacturers.

title: Refocus SBIC on small businesses and favor small manufacturers with longer-term financing
uncertainties: The law text was read on GovInfo; the small manufacturer definition is cross-referenced to section 501(e)(6) of the Small Business Investment Act, which was not opened, and the law firm summary describes it as NAICS sectors 31 to 33 with all production in the United States. The law also extends the exclusion to critical technology areas, so it does not by itself shift support away from technology firms. An SBA statement of 2026-05-21 on the signing was seen only as a search result and was removed. Other 119th Congress SBIC bills (for example S. 2223, introduced 2025-07-09) do not address manufacturers and are not events here. Whether the removal of Early Stage SBIC licensing counts as refocusing away from startups is a judgment; it is treated as a partial step.
